description: A column a rep can see, filter, sort, group and board on that is not in the database and is never written. The row declares an ordered list of buckets — each a value and the ordinary filters that define it — and the same filters answer both questions a list asks: what does this row read as, and which rows read as that. Nothing is stored on a lead or a task, so a field can be added, changed or retired at any time and no data moves. Every row is proved on real records inside a rolled-back trial before it saves: buckets that could claim one record twice, or a declaration whose column and filter would name different rows, are refused with the collision named. Ships disabled — a saved row changes nothing anywhere until Enabled is ticked.

fields.label: List
fields.description: The doctype whose list carries this field. It is the subject and the target both — the value is computed from this doctype's own columns and the field can never appear on another. It cannot be changed once saved; a field for a different list is a new row.

fields.label: Fieldname
fields.description: The name every surface addresses this field by — lower case letters, digits and underscores. It must not be a column the doctype already has, and it must not be a field declared in code. It cannot be changed once saved, because a saved view, a sort or a board naming it would be left pointing at nothing.

fields.label: Label
fields.description: What the rep sees: the column header and the entry in every menu. It is read from this row on every response, so renaming it moves all five menus at once and no saved view has to be touched.

fields.label: Order Rows Within A Bucket By
fields.description: A column of this list used to order rows INSIDE one bucket, written as a bare fieldname with no direction. Optional: without it the rows in a bucket fall back to the framework's own ordering. The buckets themselves always sort in the order they are declared below.

fields.label: Where It Is Offered
fields.description: Which menus carry the field, and whether it arrives on the list unasked. Nothing here is a permission — a rep who is not offered the field on one surface can still meet it on another.

fields.label: Surfaces
fields.description: Which menus offer the field, as a comma-separated list of: column, filter, sort, group_by, quick_filter. Left blank it is offered in all five. `column` is the column picker, which is also the Kanban board's column picker. `quick_filter` only makes the field resolvable in the filter bar — a rep still has to add it there. Removing a menu takes the field out of that menu alone and is not a permission.

fields.label: Shown By Default
fields.description: Show the column without the rep adding it. Off by default — an offered field waits to be asked for.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Nothing reads this row until this is ticked. A saved but disabled row is proved and inert: it is in no menu, on no list, in no board and in no export.

fields.label: The Declaration
fields.description: The buckets, as JSON. Order is load-bearing twice: the first bucket a record matches is the value it shows, and that same order is the order the field sorts in. A record no bucket claims shows an empty cell, which is the honest answer when the declaration does not cover it.

fields.label: Buckets (JSON)
fields.description: An ordered list of {"value", "theme", "filters"}. `value` is what the rep reads; `theme` is the badge colour (gray, blue, green, orange, red — absent or unknown reads gray); `filters` is a list of [fieldname, operator, value] on this list's own columns, all of which must hold. Example: [{"value": "Controlled", "theme": "green", "filters": [["custom_hba1c", "<", 7]]}, {"value": "Uncontrolled", "theme": "red", "filters": [["custom_hba1c", ">=", 7]]}]. Ranges are half-open (>= start, < end): an inclusive upper bound reads differently in the list than it does in a filter, and that is refused on save.

name: CRM Derived Field
